data.title: ConnectM Tech Solutions Files 8K - Entry Into Definitive Agreement >CNTM
data.description:
ConnectM Technology Solutions Inc. (CNTM) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 19, 2026.

As previously disclosed in the Annual Report on Form 10-K of ConnectM Technology Solutions, Inc. (the "Company") for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on April 16, 2026, the Company entered into a Settlement and Termination Agreement (the "Settlement Agreement") on December 29, 2025 with YA II PN, Ltd. ("Yorkville") related to the Standby Equity Purchase Agreement between the Company and Yorkville dated December 17, 2024 (the "SEPA") and the promissory note issued by the Company to Yorkville on December 17, 2024 pursuant to the SEPA evidencing the Pre-Paid Advance (as defined in the SEPA) (the "Note"). The Settlement Agreement provides for $250,000 cash payments by the Company to Yorkville on alternate Mondays, commencing December 29, 2025, applied to reduce the outstanding obligations in respect of the Pre-Paid Advance (including principal, accrued interest and any applicable premiums or fees) (the "Pre-Paid Advance Obligation"), and confirms that the $250,000 payment made on December 15, 2025 was applied first to satisfy the $187,500 deferred fee payable under the SEPA, with the remaining $62,500 applied to the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation. For each alternate Monday payment timely received, Yorkville agreed that, during the 14-day period beginning on the date of receipt, it will not deliver any Investor Notice (as defined in the SEPA) or otherwise exercise any right to cause a deemed Advance Notice under the SEPA in respect of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation.

The Settlement Agreement further provides that, if the Company consummates a firm-commitment underwritten public offering of its common stock registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, in connection with an uplisting to a national securities exchange (the "IPO"), the SEPA will be terminated effective immediately prior to the closing of the IPO, subject to (a) repayment in full of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation, (b) issuance to Yorkville of a termination fee payable in shares of common stock with an aggregate value of $175,000, valued at the public offering price per share in the IPO (the "Termination Fee Shares") and (c) delivery of customary termination and payoff documentation. Yorkville will also have a right of first refusal, for 24 months following the closing of the IPO, with respect to any future equity line of credit or similar committed equity facility, excluding any at-the-market offering program, underwritten offerings and other one-time financings not structured as a committed equity line. Upon the termination of the SEPA and the satisfaction of these conditions, each party will release the other from claims arising out of the SEPA and the related transaction documents, subject to certain exceptions.

Letter Agreement

On November 11, 2026, the Company and Yorkville entered into a letter agreement regarding Repayment of Pre-Paid Advance Obligation and Participation in the Company's Public Offering (the "Letter Agreement"), supplementing the Settlement Agreement with respect to the repayment of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation under the SEPA and the Note in connection with the IPO. The Letter Agreement also provides that the IPO may be conducted in connection with the listing of the common stock on the NYSE American.

The Letter Agreement contains the following material terms:

The "Payoff Amount" equals the unpaid principal, plus accrued and unpaid interest, plus any applicable redemption or prepayment premiums or fees relating to the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation. The parties acknowledged that as of November 11, 2026, the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation consisted of principal of $600,000 and accrued and unpaid interest of $56,219, totaling $656,219, with interest accruing at $296 per day after that date.

Within three business days after the closing of the IPO, the Company will pay Yorkville the total Payoff Amount, calculated as of the date of payment, including interest accrued through the date of payment (the "Final Payment"), (a) through the Participation Payment described below, if any, and (b) as to the remainder, in cash by wire transfer. The parties agreed that payment of the Final Payment in accordance with the Letter Agreement will satisfy the payment timing requirement and the repayment condition to the termination of the SEPA under the Settlement Agreement.

If the parties so elect, the Company may allocate to Yorkville up to $250,000 of the securities offered in the IPO at the public offering price, to be paid for by Yorkville through a reduction of an equal amount of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation (the "Participation Payment"). Yorkville's indication of interest is not binding. No securities may be sold, and no offer to buy may be accepted, before the registration statement for the IPO is declared effective, and the underwriters may allocate fewer or no securities to Yorkville. The Company's payment obligations under the Letter Agreement do not depend on whether Yorkville purchases securities in the IPO.

The maturity date for the Note was extended to January 15, 2027. The Company ratified and confirmed the Note and acknowledged that it is indebted to Yorkville under the Note in the amounts set forth in the Letter Agreement.

The Company, on behalf of itself and its subsidiaries, agents, attorneys, shareholders, advisors, officers, directors, employees, affiliates, predecessors, successors and assigns, acknowledged that it has no offsets, defenses, claims, or counterclaims against Yorkville, its investment manager or their respective related parties with respect to the Note, the SEPA, the Settlement Agreement, the transactions contemplated by the Letter Agreement or otherwise, and waived and released any such offsets, defenses, claims or counterclaims, whether known or unknown, arising through the date of the Letter Agreement.

Except as expressly set forth in the Letter Agreement, all other terms of the Settlement Agreement remain in full force and effect, including the provisions regarding the termination of the SEPA, the issuance of the Termination Fee Shares, and Yorkville's right of first refusal.

The foregoing descriptions of the Settlement Agreement and the Letter Agreement do not purport to be complete and are qualified in their entirety by reference to the full text of the Settlement Agreement, a copy of which was filed as Exhibit 10.93 to the Company's Form S-1, as amended, originally filed with the SEC on January 16, 2026, and the Letter Agreement, a copy of which is filed as Exhibit 10.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K, each of which is incorporated herein by reference.

This Current Report on Form 8-K does not constitute an offer to sell, or the solicitation of an offer to buy, any securities, nor shall there be any sale of securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. There can be no assurance that the IPO will be consummated on the terms described herein or at all.

Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements

This Current Report on Form 8-K contains forward-looking statements. The Company has based these forward-looking statements on its current expectations and projections about future events. All statements, other than statements of present or historical fact included in this Current Report on Form 8-K, regarding the proposed IPO, the potential listing of the common stock on the NYSE American, the termination of the SEPA, the issuance of the Termination Fee Shares, the repayment of the Pre-Paid Advance Obligation and the Note, including the amount, timing and form of the Final Payment and any Participation Payment, the Company's future financial performance, strategy, future operations, prospects, plans and objectives of management are forward-looking statements. data.title: Budget carrier Citilink Indonesia expects improved December travel despite high jet fuel prices
data.description:
Budget carrier Citilink Indonesia sees improved fourth-quarter demand for flights and higher bookings for December compared with the same month a year earlier, although fuel prices remain challenging, CEO Darsito Hendroseputro said on Thursday.

A subsidiary of national carrier Garuda Indonesia, Citilink expects improved revenue for December as "the economy gets better and people want to travel more," he said in an interview on the sidelines of a transport conference at the International Civil Aviation Organization in Montreal.

  • Hendroseputro: Demand in September slumped due to high jet fuel prices linked to the war in Iran

  • Airline has needed to trim other costs like travel expenses to cut losses

  • Some Asia-Pacific airlines face growing exposure to elevated jet fuel prices as older hedging contracts expire

data.title: Ross Stores Raises Outlook Again on Strong Foot Traffic
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Ross Stores once again raised its profit outlook for the year after posting higher quarterly sales, as the retailer attracts more shoppers to its stores.

However, the retailer's outlook for the current quarter, where it stuck to its guidance for same-store sales growth while trimming its per-share profit expectations, fell below Wall Street expectations, which weighed on shares.

For the third-quarter, Ross reported a profit of $606.3 million, or $1.91 a share, up from $511.9 million, or $1.58 a share, a year earlier. Analysts polled by FactSet expected earnings of $1.88 a share.

Revenue rose 12% to $6.26 billion, above Wall Street estimates for $6.25 billion. Same-store sales increased 8%, driven by higher customer traffic. Analysts expected 8.1% growth.

Headed into the holiday season, Ross is maintaining its outlook for fourth-quarter same-store sales growth of 4% to 5%. Analysts were already ahead of that range, modeling the key metric to rise 5.1%.

Ross lowered its fourth-quarter earnings per share guidance to $2.16 and $2.25 from $2.17 to $2.26. That still falls below analyst expectations of $2.27 a share.

For the full year, Ross now expects earnings per share between $8.75 and $8.84, up from its previous forecast of $8.61 to $8.77.

Ross opened 51 new stores during the quarter, completing its full-year opening plan of 115 new locations.

In after-hours trading Thursday, Ross stock fell nearly 7% to $204.51.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: SEC's Daly sees no chance of launching 3x, 5x single-stock leveraged ETFs
data.description:
By Suzanne McGee

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is unlikely to approve exchange-traded funds that offer leverage of three to five times the exposure to the daily performance of individual stocks, according to Brian Daly, director of the agency's division of investment management.

While several issuers have pending SEC applications for such products, Daly told a Bloomberg conference on Thursday that the law clearly limits leverage on such ETF products to double the performance of the single underlying stock.

"For us, that's more or less where the discussion ends," Daly said. "The law says 2x; we are stopping at 2x."

During the US government shutdown in October 2025, asset managers filed dozens of applications for highly leveraged ETFs, seeking to capitalize on a temporary fast-track approval process the agency introduced while staff were furloughed. But Daly told Reuters at the time that it was unclear whether the products would comply with an SEC derivatives rule which generally limits leverage to 2x.

Some issuers have disputed the SEC's interpretation of that rule, arguing instead that a different rule that establishes how to calculate leverage actually applies in this instance.

The SEC this year sought ‌public feedback on "novel" ETFs, including leverage products, in a process that wrapped up in September. This rapidly growing category of products ranges from those using derivatives to obtain leverage, cushion losses or generate income, to those linked to cryptocurrency and prediction market contracts.

Daly cautioned on Thursday not to expect an announcement of sweeping changes following those comments, although incremental changes may show up as part of broader shifts in SEC policies or thinking.

"We are not going to come out with a big bang," Daly said. The system that reviews filings "works well. This system works well. These products work well. We do not need to rewrite the rules of the game."

data.title: ADP Acquires AI-Powered ZenBusiness
data.description:
ROSELAND (dpa-AFX) - Automatic Data Processing, Inc. (ADP) has acquired ZenBusiness, an AI-powered business formation and compliance platform that has helped over one million entrepreneurs start their businesses.

The acquisition expands ADP's services for small businesses, covering business formation, insurance, payroll, compliance, HR and workforce management.

ADP CEO Maria Black said the company has supported small businesses for over 77 years by helping them manage regulations and grow their businesses.

She welcomed ZenBusiness to ADP, highlighting that the combined company will provide entrepreneurs with tools to manage business operations, payroll, compliance, HR and workforce needs from the start.

On Nasdaq, the shares are trading at $301.19 after hours. The shares closed Thursday's trading 1.43 percent down.
